title: Kioxia LD4 E1.L QLC NVMe SSD Announced
gist: Kioxia introduced its first E1.L form factor SSD, the LD4 series using BiCS FLASH generation 8 QLC, at 15.36TB and 30.72TB with a validated architecture up to 122.88TB, aimed at read-intensive hyperscale 1U servers. It remains PCIe Gen5, and the author expects QLC storage to move to Gen6 more slowly than GPU-node drives.

insights.claim: Kioxia's LD4 is its first E1.L form factor SSD, built with BiCS FLASH generation 8 QLC and targeted at read-intensive hyperscale workloads in high-density 1U scale-out servers.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: QLC in E1.L pushes capacity per 1U for read-heavy hyperscale tiers.
insights.locator: Kioxia has introduced its first E1.L

insights.claim: The LD4 launches at 15.36TB and 30.72TB, with an architecture validated for up to 122.88TB; it is a single-port design that is apparently already sampling.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Signals a roadmap to very high capacities within the same form factor.

insights.claim: E1.L is 9.5mm thick and 318.75mm long, a shape designed to fit more flash capacity into a 1U chassis by extending depth for longer PCBs and more NAND sites.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Form factor, not just NAND density, determines 1U capacity.

insights.claim: Although PCIe Gen6 servers have started to arrive, the LD4 is still PCIe Gen5, and the author senses storage applications, especially QLC NAND, will transition to Gen6 more slowly than the drives in GPU nodes.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Gen6 storage adoption will lag AI-node SSD adoption.

insights.claim: The author says E1.L matters for 1U servers because two 30.72TB E1.L drives take little front panel area, which helps front-cabled servers and ORv3 racks that put power, liquid cooling and interconnect at the rear.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: E1.L offers a space-efficient capacity option versus E3.L and E2 in dense racks.
insights.locator: While folks are looking at E3.L and E2
